edge.mechanism: Incremental AI data-center electric load cannot be served before utilities and system operators complete large-load interconnection studies, reliability planning, and any required transmission or grid-capacity additions.

evidence.summary: DOE's LBNL-backed report estimated U.S. data-center electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023 and projected 325 to 580 TWh by 2028, with AI applications identified as a driver of load growth.
NERC's FERC filing documented rapidly increasing data-center-type loads and the resulting need for grid planning, reliability analysis, information sharing, and large-load integration work.
Arcosa reported record utility-and-related-structures backlog of $648.1 million, up 49% from the start of 2026.
